Marniy rested her hands on the counter while she listened to Cecilia. She had the same regal look as her daughter, and pointed ears to match that barely showed through thick, wavy hair.
Elena watched Cecilia and Marniy chat out of the corner of her eye while putting away the food they brought. She knew her love would make a good impression, but her Mama was one to chat. Marniy asked the usual questions, 'What do you do for work, Oh my a soldier!', and so on, all in all being very kind. Elena rejoined the conversation since everything was put away, giving Cecilia a peck on the cheek.
Veronika and Susana removed to the rear porch to smoke. It would be a couple of hours till their families came by. Veronika had brushed her hair, securing it with a few pins. She wore a dark, floral patterned skirt and a fur coat. Zana's hair was braided and topped with a fur hat, and she had a traditional dress + coat. Nika pulled two smokes from her pack, handing one to Zana and lighting her own.
[i]"Ah, the country air, almost free of millstink. It is nice, isn't it, Z?"[/i] she asked plainly.
[i]"You know I get so used to the air being poison, now that you mention it."[/i]
The two held straight faces before breaking into chuckles.
[i]"Maybe. Maybe we'll figure out if we're coming or going, but my job has been hard, Nashka,"[/i] Susana paused to take a drag, [i]"It's good to get away from it, but I'm wading through red tape! I mean running chemical waste through a leechfield, and that's normal out in Andrudin."[/i] she shook her head, pinching the bridge of her nose.
[i]"Propping up an illegal weapons exchange is a new one for me."
"Regime change has a complicated follow-through."[/i][/quote]

Cecilia smiled. She felt welcome, and was very appreciative of Marniy's openness to her presence. She spoke with her for a while before offering to help out with dinner if needed.

On a certain afternoon there were two men and a woman that kept closely together throughout the quiet journey towards Boseong-gun. They briefly chatted with one another in the car on that trip but did not seem to offer much except vague pleasantries on the circumstances of the trip therein.

"And remember", the man in the mlitary outfit said, leaning back towards the Sanguinians behind him. "that we are in a quiet and foreign land that understands very little of the cause of socialism. We're not here as friends of Minhokae, just pragmatic allies."

"You're too uptight, Comrade Cui." said the Sanguinian with the strange red hair, laughing quietly to himself as the car brought itself to a stop by that old house. "Socialists need to befriend non-socialists too, you know? How else are we supposed to spread the revolution?"

[i]"Quello che ha detto!"[/i] applauded the glasses-wearing woman, the golden Chi-Rho on her shoulder shining brilliantly as the trio stepped out and walked beneath the sweltering July heat. 

Moving quickly to avoid sweating, the three entered the house, and would immediately shake hands with the king. Cui Jin, the man in the military outfit, would bow to the king deferentially as a mark of respect, not for the king's high rank but rather just out of customary Qianxun courtesy. The two Sanguinians wouldn't bother, with such acts of deference existing far beyond their system.

"You chose an odd spot for a meetup, Minhokeans." Argo Lo Pilato, the red-haired one, would mutter quickly after the initial exchange of pleasantries, taking a moment to look around him, casing and observing the state of the building that they were in. "I understand wanting to be discrete for geopolitical reasons, but at a certain point this discreteness leads up to places that I really wouldn't want to be in, heh..."

Romariian News Network Live Broadcasting
---------------------------
Emergency Address by Mario Mario
---------------------------

[i]The broadcast begins. As the Camera stabilizes, the President (not the Monarch, ok) of Imperium Romae Marii is seen with papers in his hands, behind a lectern, bearing the coat of arms of Imperium Romae Marii.[/i]

"Good afternoon, everyone. This is the President (not the monarch, ok) of Imperium Romae Marii, Mario Mario, addressing the nation regarding recent developments."

[i]Reads the paper[/i]

"Ok, first, concerning the situation in Zuiden Island. The government has decided to proceed with the withdrawal of all naval assets from the region, following the recognition of Yulandburgs claim on Yesterday. This decision was made to reduce external tensions and prevent further escalation. We will also refer to the island by its International name, Xahu Island. We will not withdraw from Isle Duckie, Isle Long, and Tres Isoles as these islands are not colonies."

"Secondly, we have received a proposal from the Nederlandse Staat regarding the protection of citizens of Dutch ethnicity within our borders. While the proposal may seem weird, as it suggests arming the Dutch minority with weapons to protect themselves, it is currently under review. I will admit, it sounds somewhat extreme, but given the situation, it is also quite understandable?"

[i]Shifts the paper[/i]

"Finally, regarding the April 12th incident in Yoshiland. The government will comply with international demands and is prepared to hand over any high-ranking military personnel involved for investigation and trial. These will be..."

[i]Looks down at document, and stops talking[/i]

"one moment."

[i]Mario is visibly confused[/i]

"There um, appears to be no high-ranking officers listed as involved."

"I...um.."

[i]Turns slightly away from the camera[/i]

"Luigi?"

[i]Off-mic voice, slightly audible.[/i]

"Luigi, is this list a joke? There are no high-ranking personnel in the RISF?"

[i]Luigi walks in, and looks at the document[/i]

Luigi:  
"No, thats not a joke Mario. Its a decentralized force, everyone knows that! Did you forget?"

Mario:  
"oh yeah!"

"That would also explain how they managed to mistake mustard gas for tear gas, no one was there to-!"

[i]Luigi interrupts Mario, and he points at the camera.[/i]

Luigi:  
"Wait, is this live?"

Mario:  
"Ye... oh crap-"

[i]Broadcast abruptly cuts to static[/i]

---------------------------
We will be right back.
---------------------------
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=the Movement]
Romariian News Network
---------------------------
Independence Movements in Lil' Warszawa and Lil' Geranora Rise
---------------------------

Following the recent naval withdrawal from Zuiden Island earlier today, independence movements in Lil' Warszawa and Lil' Geranora have risen once again, marking the second wave of protests since their integration into Imperium Romae Marii in 2027.

Historically, both provinces were part of independent nations, with Lil' Warszawa formerly belonging to Wielka Warszawa, and Lil' Geranora to Geranora. Both nations collapsed under unclear circumstances, leading to the division of their former territories between Romariia and (later) Arelia.

In recent days, protests and riots have intensified across both regions, with demonstrators calling for full independence from Romariia and the reformation of their former nations. Some groups have gone further, expressing ambitions to reclaim territories currently under Arelian control.

Local leaders and activists cite several reasons for the renewed unrest, including cultural differences, dissatisfaction with central governance, and growing concerns over the countrys political instability. The recent withdrawal from Zuiden Island has also been interpreted by many as a sign of government weakness, further encouraging separatist sentiment.

Reports indicate that clashes between protesters and local authorities have already occurred, with several injuries and even deaths reported. In some areas, protesters have begun organizing into loosely structured extremist groups.

Experts warn that if the situation continues to escalate, these independence movements could evolve into full-scale separatist conflicts, further fragmenting the nation at a time when it is already facing significant internal and external pressures.

There are also concerns that any attempt to reclaim territory from Arelia could risk drawing the neighboring state into the conflict, potentially expanding the crisis beyond Romariias borders.

The RISF has not yet been deployed due to caution.
[/spoiler]

Romariian News Network
---------------------------
New Political Party Gains Popularity
---------------------------

Today, a new political party has risen in popularity across Imperium Romae Marii, marking the first major emergence of a new political force since the nations establishment in 2005.

The political party, known as the Coalition for the Establishment of the Republic of Romariia, is led by Bob Dansic, a figure who, while not widely recognized by the general public until recently, is no stranger to politics.

The party has called for the complete removal of Mario Mario and his family from power, as well as the complete restructuring of the current political system. According to statements released by the coalition, their primary goals include the establishment of a true republican system, the restoration of political accountability, and the stabilization of the nation through democratic reforms.

The coalition has also expressed strong opposition to both foreign intervention and the government's handling of recent crises, especially about the Xahu Island dispute, arguing that the current leadership has failed to maintain internal stability while simultaneously weakening the nations position on the international stage.

In addition, the party has called for:
[list][*]the protection of all religious and minority groups under a neutral state policy  
[*] the prevention of further territorial concessions to foreign powers  
[*] the prevention of any provinces seceding
[*]and the restoration of public trust through transparent governance  [/list]

The party claims it was formed in response to what it describes as a complete breakdown of leadership following recent events, including the Yoshiland incident, increasing foreign pressure, and the disappearance of Marietta Mario.

Public response has been mixed. Some citizens have expressed support for the coalition, viewing it as a potential solution to the nations growing instability. Others remain skeptical, questioning whether a newly formed political group can realistically navigate the rapidly deteriorating situation, with some observers noting the unusually rapid organization and outreach of the coalition, raising questions about possible backing from undisclosed groups.

Analysts warn that the sudden rise of such a movement may further fragment the already unstable political landscape, potentially accelerating the countrys descent into wider conflict.
[/spoiler]
